messages:
Anya Patel: Heads-up: experimenting with a compatibility queuing shim that diffs outgoing /v2 model payloads and either 1) transform inline, 2) queue+defer, or 3) pass-through. Want to capture tradeoffs before RFC.
Ravi Shah: Queue+defer sounds safer for strict parity consumers but how does it affect streaming/backpressure?
Marta Ruiz: If we defer, we need a clear contract: clients get a short 202-like meta-frame with a request_id and `compat_status: deferred`. Then final fields arrive as a follow-up event.
Anya Patel: Exactly. Proposal: new header `X-Compat-Behavior: transform|defer|passthrough`. Default `transform` (best-effort).
Ravi Shah: Transform = lowest latency but lossy in edge cases. Defer = preserves exact fields but introduces asynchronous completion semantics. Passthrough = fastest but breaks clients expecting old fields.
Marta Ruiz: Operational constraints: deferred mode requires durable queueing (etcd-backed or redis streams). Need visibility into queue depth and per-tenant backlog to avoid silent outages.
sre-bot: queue-health-check: compat-queue: healthy. depth=24 per-tenant-highwater=3 alert=false
Anya Patel: For streaming we can do hybrid: stream tokens as they arrive (passthrough) and send a `compat_frame` at the end, or if client requests `block_until_compat=true` via header, hold stream.
Ravi Shah: Holding streams is painful for UI clients (spinner). We should make `block_until_compat` opt-in and default false. Also add `X-Compat-ETA-ms` in the initial meta-frame so clients can decide to render partial view.
Marta Ruiz: Agree. Telemetry we need: `compat_invoked`, `compat_mode`, `compat_latency_ms`, `compat_queue_depth`, `compat_retry_count`, `compat_transform_errors`. Link to schema: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/compat-schema.md
Anya Patel: Canary plan: internal + dev tenants in `defer` for 2h, watch `compat_latency_ms.p99 < 500ms` and `missing_fields_rate < 0.2%`. If queue depth per-tenant > 500, immediate rollback.
Ravi Shah: Also enforce resource isolation: `defer` mode should be schedulable to dedicated workers for enterprise tenants that buy stricter SLOs. Otherwise shared workers could starve.
Marta Ruiz: On retries: transform attempts should be idempotent; deferred tasks must be deduped via request_id. Add a signed request_id header so private deployments can audit.
Anya Patel: For private deployments we expose a config flag `compat.queue.backend` = {redis,etcd,kafka} and a `compat.queue.max_age_ms`.
Ravi Shah: Runbook snippets: if `compat_transform_errors` > 1% in 10m, flip canary -> rollback, page on-call. If `compat_queue_depth` trending up for >= 5m, scale workers or pause non-critical tenants.
sre-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure RBAC for queue admin, set alarm for depth>1000, create grafana dashboard `compat/queue`
Marta Ruiz: Security: transformations touch PII fields. Ensure mapping transforms run through redaction pipeline and never log raw PII.
Anya Patel: Good catch. We'll add `compat_redacted=true` tag in telemetry and double-check tests.
Ravi Shah: One more thing: clients that rely on sequence numbers in v1 must see stable message ids. If we defer and emit a follow-up frame, preserve upstream sequence via `compat_seq` header.
Marta Ruiz: I'll add an integration test plan that simulates slow transformers and high-concurrency deferred loads to validate backpressure + retry logic.
Anya Patel: Next steps: I'll draft the short follow-up RFC with header names, telemetry events, and canary gates. Ravi, can you list the infra work (queue choice + metrics)?
Ravi Shah: On it. Also tagging @deploy-bot to schedule the internal canary for 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z.
deploy-bot: Scheduled job: compat-queue-canary -> prod-canary at 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
Marta Ruiz: Final note: make sure client SDKs get a minor bump that recognizes `compat_frame` and `compat_status` to avoid noisy bugs.
Anya Patel: Agreed. Will include in RFC compatibility matrix and SDK changelog notes.
